key_insight: AP-OOD replaces simple average pooling with a learned attention-pooling mechanism over token embeddings to produce a single, more informative OOD score — leveraging token-level signals to better separate in-distribution and out-of-distribution inputs.
problem_solved: How to aggregate high-dimensional token embeddings from language models into a single scalar OOD score that reliably identifies out-of-distribution text, while preserving interpretability and using limited supervision.
method: Learned attention pooling: train a lightweight attention module that assigns importance weights to token embeddings and pools them into a single representation for scoring.
Semi-supervised calibration: use limited in-/out-of-distribution supervision (or proxy negatives) to shape attention weights and the final OOD scoring function without retraining the backbone LM.

Token-level contributions: compute per-token OOD contributions (attention × token score) to enable interpretability and localized anomaly signals, and derive a final scalar OOD score from the pooled representation.
impact: Provides practitioners a plug-in, interpretable OOD detector that improves sensitivity to localized anomalies in text, is compatible with pre-trained language models, and reduces reliance on blunt average-based aggregation for safer deployment.
visual_elements: Model diagram: token embeddings → attention pooling layer → pooled representation → scalar OOD score (annotate trainable attention weights).
Text heatmap: example sentence with token-level attention/OOD contributions highlighted to show where the model detects anomalies.
Performance sketch: bar or line chart comparing AP-OOD vs average pooling and other baselines on standard OOD metrics (e.g., AUROC) — emphasize relative improvement without numeric claims.
Training flowchart: semi-supervised setup showing in-distribution, limited OOD examples/proxies, and how they shape attention calibration.
paper_title: AP-OOD: Attention Pooling for Out-of-Distribution Detection
paper_authors: Claus Hofmann, Christian Huber, Bernhard Lehner, Daniel Klotz, Sepp Hochreiter
